initialize.instructions: Open modes, configure child options, and supervise a staged program.

tools.description: The engine's layer stack, bottom to top: every module at each height, with its tier. A layer may see every layer below it and none above it, so this table is what decides which module may include which. The programs are listed separately - they are what links modules and nothing links them. Call module_may_link to ask about one edge.
tools.name: layer_table

tools.description: One module or program: which layer and tier it is, every first-party target it links, and everything that links it. `linkedBy` is what would have to be rebuilt and reviewed if this module's interface changed. With no name, every module in layer order.

name.description: The module or program. Omit for all of them.

tools.name: module_get

tools.description: Whether one module is allowed to link another, and why. This is the question the architecture check answers, decided here from the same two rules: a tier may link shared and its own tier, and a layer may see every layer below it and none above it. Ask before writing an include - an edge that runs upward is refused at configure time and the fix is almost never to widen the rule.
tools.name: module_may_link

tools.description: The most recent lines this program has logged, newest last. Filter by minimum level and by category - a category is one area of the engine, usually one module, and log_level lists the ones this build registers. Only the last 1024 lines are kept, and `dropped` says how many scrolled off before the oldest one shown.

category.description: Only lines from this area. Default all of them.

level.description: The lowest severity to include. Default trace.

lines.description: How many lines at most. Default 50, capped at 1024.

tools.name: log_tail

tools.description: Reads or changes what this program logs, while it runs. With no argument it lists every category the build has registered and the severity floor each is at. `set` takes the same text the engine.log-level setting does: a bare level for everything, or comma-separated category=level overrides, or both - `warning,net=trace`. Statements below the compiled floor were removed by the preprocessor and cannot be switched on.

set.description: A level, or category=level terms, or both.

tools.name: log_level

tools.description: Every counter, gauge and distribution this process has recorded. A counter accumulates and is drained once a frame, so its value is a rate; a gauge is a level as last set; a histogram carries a mean, a maximum and nearest-rank percentiles over its recent window, which is what says whether a server holding its tick rate on average is still missing a fiftieth of its ticks. Times are nanoseconds. Reading changes nothing.

prefix.description: Only names starting with this. Default all of them.

tools.name: metrics_read

tools.description: Pure data-factory capability discovery. Reports this host's callable MCP operations and their schemas, and names unsupported proposed capture capabilities instead of guessing from renderer internals. It does not create, load, reset, or mutate a world.
tools.name: negotiate

tools.description: Moves the mouse pointer to client coordinates through this program's input boundary.
tools.name: emulate_mouse_move

tools.description: Clicks, presses, or releases a mouse button at client coordinates through this program's input boundary. Omit down for one complete click.
tools.name: emulate_click

tools.description: Turns the mouse wheel by a signed number of vertical notches through this program's input boundary.
tools.name: emulate_mouse_wheel

tools.description: Presses, releases, or taps one named keyboard key through this program's input boundary. Omit down for one complete key press.
tools.name: emulate_key

tools.description: Sends UTF-8 text through this program's input boundary.
tools.name: emulate_text

tools.description: List launcher modes, the open form, and the supervised child's current state.
tools.name: launcher_status

tools.description: Open a launcher mode and its form. Use launcher_status to see available mode ids.
tools.name: launcher_open_mode

tools.description: Set one declared option on the open mode. Values may contain several entries for repeatable options.
tools.name: launcher_set_option

tools.description: Start the open mode with the current form options.
tools.name: launcher_launch

tools.description: Request a polite stop of the supervised child.
tools.name: launcher_stop

tools.description: Close the launcher and stop its supervised child. Also ends headless MCP-only sessions.
tools.name: launcher_quit
